## Overview

Input is the single-line text field: a 56 px container holding a label, the entered value, and optional leading and trailing icons, a prefix, and supporting text beneath. It follows [Material 3 text fields](https://m3.material.io/components/text-fields/specs) in both of Material's styles:

- **Outlined** (default). A 1 px outline on the page background. Once the field has a value or focus, the label floats up and cuts a notch into the top edge. Use it for forms.
- **Filled**. A tinted container with an active indicator along the bottom edge. The floated label stays inside the container, above the value. It carries more visual weight, so keep it for standalone entry points such as a hotel or city search on a plain surface.

Do not mix the two styles within one form.

**Variant axes.** 4 axes across 32 variants:

- **Style**: Outlined, Filled. Default `Outlined`.
- **Value**: Empty, Populated. Default `Empty`.
- **State**: Default, Hover, Focus, Disabled. Default `Default`.
- **Intent**: Default, Error. Default `Default`.

`Value` decides where the label sits. It rests inside an empty, unfocused field and floats as soon as the field is populated *or* focused. Focusing an empty field therefore floats the label and reveals the placeholder and caret, as Material does. `Value` is named so it cannot be confused with `Style=Filled`.

`State` covers Material's mandatory text-field states. There is **no Pressed state**: pressing a text field focuses it, so the pressed frame is the Focus frame. Every state combines with `Intent=Error` except Disabled, which renders neutral (see Accessibility → Precedence).

### Composition

- **Icon slots.** The Leading Icon and Trailing Icon slots are instance-swap properties. Their preferred values are the 20 `Icon / *` components in the **Input icons** frame on the same page. These are Material icons, each a single `Glyph` vector.
- **Error icon.** The error variants default their trailing slot to `Icon / error`. Every other variant defaults it to `Icon / cancel` (clear).
- **Examples.** The page also holds an **Examples** section of travel patterns built from instances; see Examples below.

## API

> `State` is design-only. `Hover` and `Focus` exist so a mock can show them. In code they are `:hover` and `:focus-visible` / `:focus-within`, owned by the component. Only `State=Disabled` maps to a prop. `Value` is not a prop either; it follows from whether `value` is empty.

| Property | Type | Values | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | string | (string) | – | Required. Always visible: resting in the field, or floated. Never replaced by the placeholder. |
| `value` | string | (string) | `""` | Empty → Figma `Value=Empty`; non-empty → `Value=Populated`. |
| `placeholder` | string | (string) | `none` | Shown only while the field is empty **and** focused. Use it for a format hint (`DD/MM/YYYY`), never for the label. |
| `variant` | enum | outlined \| filled | `outlined` | Maps to Figma `Style`. |
| `invalid` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Maps to Figma `Intent=Error`. Recolours the outline/indicator, label, caret, trailing icon and supporting text. Exposes `aria-invalid="true"`. |
| `supportingText` | string | (string) | `none` | Hint under the field. When `invalid`, this slot carries the error message. |
| `prefix` | string | (string) | `none` | Fixed, non-editable text before the value (`+91`, `₹`). Shown only when the label has floated. |
| `leadingIcon` | icon | (icon) | `none` | Describes the field (phone, calendar, search). Stays neutral in the error state. |
| `trailingIcon` | icon | (icon) | `none` | An action (clear, show password, open picker) or the error glyph. |
| `disabled` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Applies the disabled treatment and makes the field non-interactive. |
| `readOnly` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Not modelled in Figma. For picker triggers (destination, dates, travellers), use the Default state with no caret. |

### Figma-only properties

| Figma property | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Label` | TEXT | `"Label"` | Drives all three label nodes (resting, floated in the Filled style, and the notch label), so the label only needs editing once. |
| `Input text` | TEXT | `"Input text"` | The value. It is named `Input text` because the variant axis already owns the name `Value`. |
| `Placeholder` | TEXT | `"Placeholder"` | Visible only in `Value=Empty, State=Focus`. |
| `Prefix` | TEXT | `"+91"` | Placeholder copy. |
| `Supporting text` | TEXT | `"Supporting text"` | Placeholder copy. |
| `Show Leading Icon` | BOOLEAN | `false` | |
| `Show Trailing Icon` | BOOLEAN | `false` | |
| `Show Prefix` | BOOLEAN | `false` | |
| `Show Supporting Text` | BOOLEAN | `true` | |
| `Leading Icon` | INSTANCE_SWAP | `Icon / search` | Preferred values: the Input icons frame. |
| `Trailing Icon` | INSTANCE_SWAP | `Icon / cancel` | The error variants override it to `Icon / error`. |

### Examples

The **Examples** section on the Figma page is built entirely from Input instances (36 of them), plus Button instances where a pattern needs an action:

| Card | What it shows |
|---|---|
| Mobile number | A `+91` prefix and a phone icon; the error message replaces the hint in the same slot. |
| Login | Username, then a password field with a show/hide trailing toggle, in Focus and in Error, then a primary Log in button. |
| Select destination | From / To read-only triggers with flight icons, the airport name as supporting text, and a swap button laid over the pair. |
| Select travel dates | Departure / Return side by side, with an optional return left empty. A check-in / check-out pair shows a range error. |
| Travellers & class | A summary field that opens a picker (trailing dropdown arrow), rooms and guests, and a Disabled fixed-fare case. |
| Search city or hotel | The Filled style in Empty, Focus (clear icon plus a match count) and Hover. |
| Promo code | The field beside a secondary Apply button; the error explains why the code failed. |
| Passenger details | A name pair, a Date of birth field showing a format placeholder on focus, passport number, and e-ticket email. |
| States at a glance | Every mandatory state for one field, Outlined beside Filled. |

## Structure

### Anatomy

```text
Input (component set · 492:674)
├─ Container (frame · horizontal · 56 high · children centred)
│  ├─ Outline (rectangle) · absolute, stretched · Outlined only
│  ├─ State Layer (rectangle) · absolute, stretched · Filled + Hover only
│  ├─ Leading Icon (instance) · Show Leading Icon
│  ├─ Content (frame · vertical · fills width)
│  │  ├─ Floating Label (text · body/small) · Filled, once floated
│  │  ├─ Resting Label (text · body/large) · until floated
│  │  └─ Input (frame · horizontal) · once floated
│  │     ├─ Prefix (frame) → Prefix Text · Show Prefix
│  │     ├─ Value (text · body/large) · Populated
│  │     ├─ Caret (rectangle) · Focus
│  │     └─ Placeholder (text · body/large) · Empty + Focus
│  ├─ Trailing Icon (instance) · Show Trailing Icon
│  └─ Notch Label (frame · absolute) → Notch Label Text (body/small) · Outlined, once floated
└─ Supporting (frame) → Supporting Text (body/small) · Show Supporting Text
```

Every variant has the same node tree; variants differ only in visibility, bound colours and stroke weight. That is what lets one set of text and boolean properties drive all 32.

**Why the outline is a separate rectangle.** Figma draws a frame's own stroke above its children, so a stroked Container would draw the outline straight through the floated label. The outline is its own rectangle, first in paint order, and the Notch Label is last. The notch is made by the label's `container-outlined` fill painting over the line, the same trick Material's web implementation uses with its outline gap.

**Why the Filled indicator is a stroke.** In the Filled style nothing overlaps the bottom edge, so the Container carries a bottom-only inside stroke. The Container clips its content, so the hover state layer follows the rounded top corners.

### Dimensions

`Style`, `State` and `Intent` change no measurements except the stroke weight on focus, and that stroke is drawn inside the container, so focusing never reflows the form.

| Property | Value | Token |
|---|---|---|
| Container height | 56 | `input/height` |
| Container horizontal padding | 12 | `input/padding-x` |
| Icon ↔ text column gap | 12 | `input/gap` |
| Text column inset | 4 | `input/text-inset` |
| Icon size | 24 | `input/icon-size` |
| Corner radius | 4 (all corners Outlined; top corners only Filled) | `input/radius` |
| Outline / indicator | 1 at rest, 2 focused | `input/border-width`, `input/border-width-focus` |
| Caret | 2 × 20 | `input/caret-width` |
| Prefix → value gap | 4 | `input/prefix-gap` |
| Notch padding either side of the floated label | 4 | `input/label-notch-padding` |
| Supporting text top gap / horizontal inset | 4 / 16 | `input/supporting-padding-top`, `input/supporting-padding-x` |
| Resting label, value, placeholder, prefix | 16 / 24 | `body/large/regular` |
| Floated label, supporting text | 12 / 16 | `body/small/regular` |

**Text start.** Padding (12) plus text inset (4) puts the label and value 16 px from an edge that has no icon. With a leading icon it is 12 + 24 + 12 + 4 = 52 px. Both are Material's figures. The three tokens are split this way because icons need 12 px from the edge and text needs 16; one padding value cannot give both.

**Vertical rhythm.** There is no vertical padding token. The Content column is centred in the fixed 56 px Container. For Outlined that centres the 24 px value line (16 above and below). For a floated Filled field it centres the 16 px label plus the 24 px value (8 above and below), which is Material's layout.

**Notch position.** The Notch Label sits at x 12, y −8: its 4 px padding brings the text back to x 16, and its 16 px line straddles the top edge. With a leading icon the floated label still aligns to 16, above the icon, as in Material.

## Color

Tokens are named `input/{property}-{style}-{intent}-{state}`, where `intent` is omitted for Default and `style` is omitted where both styles share a value.

### Container

| Style | Default / Hover / Focus | Disabled |
|---|---|---|
| Outlined | `input/container-outlined` → `color.bg` | same |
| Filled | `input/container-filled-default` → `color.bg-surface` | `input/container-filled-disabled` → `color.bg-surface-disabled` |

The Outlined container matches the page on purpose: the floated label's notch is painted in the same token. **Place Outlined fields on `color.bg` only.** On a tinted surface the notch would show as a white patch (see Known gaps).

**Filled hover** is a state layer, not a colour swap: `input/state-layer` (→ `color.text-primary`) at `input/state-layer-opacity-hover` (→ `opacity.state-layer-hover`, 8%). Over `#F5F5F5` it composites to `#E2E2E2`. Input is the first Cosmos component to use the hover state-layer step.

### Outline (Outlined) — `input/border-outlined-*`

| Intent | Default | Hover | Focus (2 px) | Disabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | `color.border` | `color.border-strong` | `color.border-brand` | `color.border-disabled-subtle` |
| Error | `color.border-warning-strong` | `color.border-warning-strong-hover` | `color.border-warning-strong` | (neutral disabled) |

### Active indicator (Filled) — `input/indicator-filled-*`

| Intent | Default | Hover | Focus (2 px) | Disabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Default | `color.border` | `color.border-strong` | `color.border-brand` | `color.border-disabled-strong` |
| Error | `color.border-warning-strong` | `color.border-warning-strong-hover` | `color.border-warning-strong` | (neutral disabled) |

- **The default intent steps up the neutral border ramp:** `border` at rest, `border-strong` on hover, `border-brand` at 2 px on focus. Every stroke uses a border role; none borrows a text token. The resting line is deliberately light, which costs WCAG 1.4.11 (see Accessibility → Contrast).
- **Focus in the error intent stays red.** A field the user is correcting does not flash brand.
- **The Filled disabled indicator uses `border-disabled-strong`.** `border-disabled-subtle` (`#D4D4D4`) is nearly invisible against the `#E5E5E5` disabled container.

### Text and icons

| Element | Default | Focus | Error | Disabled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Label (all three nodes) | `label-default` → `text-secondary` | `label-focus` → `text-brand` | `label-error` → `text-warning` | `label-disabled` → `text-disabled` |
| Value | `value-default` → `text-primary` | same | same | `value-disabled` → `text-disabled` |
| Placeholder | `placeholder` → `text-secondary` | – | – | – |
| Prefix | `prefix` → `text-secondary` | same | same | `value-disabled` |
| Caret | – | `caret-default` → `text-brand` | `caret-error` → `text-warning` | – |
| Leading icon | `icon-default` → `icon-secondary` | same | same (stays neutral) | `icon-disabled` |
| Trailing icon | `icon-default` → `icon-secondary` | same | `icon-error` → `icon-warning` | `icon-disabled` |
| Supporting text | `supporting-default` → `text-secondary` | same | `supporting-error` → `text-warning` | `supporting-disabled` → `text-disabled` |

Two deliberate departures from the obvious token:

- **Placeholder is `text-secondary`, not `text-tertiary`.** Tertiary is the semantic tier's placeholder colour, but at 4.35:1 on the Filled container it misses 4.5:1. The placeholder is only visible once the label has floated, so sharing the label colour causes no confusion.
- **Icons are `icon-secondary`, not `icon-tertiary`.** `icon-tertiary` is described as the input-adornment colour, but at 2.58:1 it fails the 3:1 that a meaningful icon (a password toggle, a clear button) needs.

## Focus

Focus is carried by three simultaneous changes, none of which reflow the field:

1. The outline or indicator thickens from 1 px to 2 px and turns `color.border-brand` (red in the error intent).
2. The label floats, if it had not already, and turns `color.text-brand`.
3. A 2 px caret appears in the same colour.

There is no separate focus ring. That matches Material, and unlike Radio's state layer it meets WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11: the 2 px brand outline is 5.12:1 against `color.bg` and 4.69:1 against the Filled container. Material's web implementation shows the same indicator for pointer focus and keyboard focus, and so should Cosmos. Style `:focus-within` on the field wrapper, not only `:focus-visible`.

## Accessibility

### Contrast

Computed from the resolved hex values. Disabled pairs are exempt from WCAG 1.4.3 and 1.4.11 and are not listed.

| Pair | Ratio | Required | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outline `#D4D4D4` on `#FFFFFF` | 1.48:1 | 3:1 (1.4.11) | **Fail — accepted deviation** |
| Outline hover `#737373` on `#FFFFFF` | 4.74:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Outline focus `#0067E8` on `#FFFFFF` | 5.12:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Outline error `#C10007` on `#FFFFFF` | 6.42:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Outline error hover `#E7000B` on `#FFFFFF` | 4.77:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Indicator `#D4D4D4` on Filled `#F5F5F5` | 1.36:1 | 3:1 | **Fail — accepted deviation** |
| Indicator hover `#737373` on hovered Filled `#E2E2E2` | 3.66:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Indicator focus `#0067E8` on `#F5F5F5` | 4.69:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Indicator error `#C10007` on `#F5F5F5` | 5.89:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Indicator error hover `#E7000B` on `#E2E2E2` | 3.68:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Label `#525252` on `#FFFFFF` / `#F5F5F5` / `#E2E2E2` | 7.81 / 7.17 / 6.03:1 | 4.5:1 (1.4.3) | Pass |
| Label focus `#0067E8` on `#FFFFFF` / `#F5F5F5` | 5.12 / 4.69:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Label error `#C10007` on `#FFFFFF` / `#F5F5F5` / `#E2E2E2` | 6.42 / 5.89 / 4.96:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Value `#0A0A0A` on `#FFFFFF` / `#F5F5F5` | 19.80 / 18.16:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Placeholder `#525252` on `#F5F5F5` | 7.17:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Supporting `#525252` on `#FFFFFF` | 7.81:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Supporting error `#C10007` on `#FFFFFF` | 6.42:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Icon `#525252` on `#FFFFFF` / `#F5F5F5` / `#E2E2E2` | 7.81 / 7.17 / 6.03:1 | 3:1 (1.4.11) | Pass |
| Icon error `#C10007` on `#FFFFFF` | 6.42:1 | 3:1 | Pass |

**The resting field boundary does not meet WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.11.** This is a known, accepted deviation, chosen for a quieter resting field. The outline (`color.border`, 1.48:1 on white) and the Filled indicator (1.36:1 on `#F5F5F5`) are both below the 3:1 that identifies a component. The Filled container adds nothing (`#F5F5F5` is 1.09:1 against the page). What still makes the field findable at rest is the label inside it (7.81:1), and every interactive state clears 3:1: hover 4.74 / 3.66:1, focus 5.12 / 4.69:1, error 6.42 / 5.89:1. To restore conformance, repoint `border-outlined-default` and `indicator-filled-default` to `color.border-strong` (4.74 / 4.35:1). Hover then needs a darker step than `border-strong`, which the semantic tier does not have.

The tightest passing pair is the Filled error indicator on hover, at 3.68:1, with the Filled hover indicator close behind at 3.66:1. Re-measure both if the neutral or warning ramps are re-tinted.

### Semantics

| Platform | Mapping |
|---|---|
| Web | Native `<input>` with a `<label for>`. Do not use the placeholder as a label, and do not use a visually hidden label with the floated one as decoration: the visible label *is* the `<label>`. Point `aria-describedby` at the supporting text. When invalid, set `aria-invalid="true"` and have the supporting text carry the message. Use the right `type` and `inputmode` / `autocomplete` (`tel` + `inputmode="numeric"` for mobile, `current-password`, `email`, `bday`). The prefix is visual; include it in the accessible description or the submitted value, not in the label. |
| iOS / VoiceOver | `UITextField` / SwiftUI `TextField` with `accessibilityLabel` = label and `accessibilityHint` = supporting text. When invalid, announce the message with `UIAccessibility.post(.announcement)` on validation. Use the matching `textContentType` (`.telephoneNumber`, `.password`, `.oneTimeCode`). |
| Android / TalkBack | Material `TextInputLayout` / Compose `OutlinedTextField` / `TextField`, with `label`, `supportingText` and `isError`, which TalkBack announces as "error". Use the matching `KeyboardType`. |

**Picker triggers.** From / To, dates and travellers in the examples open a sheet rather than accept typing. On the web, render them as a `<button>` styled with the Input tokens, or an `<input readonly>` with `role="combobox"`, `aria-haspopup="dialog"` and `aria-expanded`. Never use a plain focusable input that ignores typing.

**Icon buttons.** A trailing icon that does something (clear, show password) is a button with its own accessible name ("Clear", "Show password"), and it toggles `aria-pressed` for show/hide. A purely decorative leading icon is `aria-hidden`.

**Precedence.** `disabled` wins over `invalid`: an inert field does not announce an error, and every disabled variant renders neutral.

**Touch target.** At 56 px the field clears the 48 px minimum. A trailing icon button must also reach 48 × 48 in code, overhanging its 24 px glyph, without changing the layout.

## Known gaps

- **The Outlined notch assumes `color.bg` behind the field.** It works by painting `input/container-outlined` behind the floated label. On `bg-surface` or a card with a tinted fill, the notch shows as a white patch. Code should cut the outline instead of painting over it (Material web uses a notched `fieldset` / `legend`). In Figma, override the Notch Label fill if you must place an Outlined field on a tint.
- **The resting boundary fails WCAG 1.4.11 by design.** `border` at rest is 1.48:1 on white and 1.36:1 on the Filled container. It is documented under Accessibility → Contrast, with the two-token change that would restore conformance.
- **Outlined Disabled is close to Outlined Default.** Disabled uses `border-disabled-subtle`, which resolves to the same `#D4D4D4` as the new resting border, and the Outlined container stays white. Only the text and icon colours separate the two states. A disabled fill (`bg-surface-disabled`, as exploration 2 uses) would fix it.
- **The Filled resting indicator is faint.** At 1.36:1 against `#F5F5F5`, the one line that marks a Filled field barely shows at rest.
- **`input/height` aliases a primitive.** The semantic space scale jumps from 48 to 64, so `height` points at `spacing.56` directly. This follows the precedent of `radio/dot-size-md` → `spacing.10`.
- **The notch label's position is baked geometry.** x 12 / y −8 is not a variable-bindable property, so changing `input/height`, the label type size or `padding-x` means re-positioning the Notch Label on all 16 Outlined variants.
- **The label float is not animated.** Material animates the label between its resting and floated positions (150 ms, standard easing). No motion token exists yet.
- **There is no Size axis.** Material ships one density. Cosmos may later need a 48 px compact field for dense filters; that would add a `Size` axis and `height-*` tokens.
- **Not modelled:** multi-line / textarea, suffix text, a character counter (use the supporting-text slot for now), read-only as a state, and a prefix icon distinct from the leading icon.
- **The icon library is local to this page.** The Button page has its own six `Icon / *` components, and the 20 on this page duplicate `close` in spirit (`cancel`). They should move to a shared Icons page when one exists, so both components draw on one set.
- **No dark mode.** All three variable collections are single-mode, matching Button, Checkbox and Radio.
- **Not uSpec-generated.** This file was hand-authored next to the Figma build. Re-run the `create-component-md` flow (README → "Generating a spec for a new component") to replace it with an extracted spec.

## Token reference

48 tokens under `component.input` in `tokens/tokens.json`, mirrored 1:1 as `input/*` in the Figma `component` collection, with WEB / iOS / ANDROID code syntax set on every variable.

| Group | Count |
|---|---|
| `container-*` | 3 |
| `state-layer`, `state-layer-opacity-hover` | 2 |
| `border-outlined-*` | 7 |
| `indicator-filled-*` | 7 |
| `label-*` | 4 |
| `value-*`, `placeholder`, `prefix` | 4 |
| `caret-*` (colour) | 2 |
| `icon-*` (colour) | 3 |
| `supporting-*` (colour) | 3 |
| dimensions (`height`, `padding-x`, `text-inset`, `gap`, `prefix-gap`, `icon-size`, `radius`, `border-width`, `border-width-focus`, `caret-width`, `label-notch-padding`, `supporting-padding-top`, `supporting-padding-x`) | 13 |

Platform names follow the standard pipeline: `input/border-outlined-error-focus` → `--input-border-outlined-error-focus` (CSS) → `CosmosTokens.inputBorderOutlinedErrorFocus` (Swift / Kotlin) → `tokens.input["border-outlined-error-focus"]` (TS default export, nested by group).

Input added **no new semantic or primitive tokens**. It is the first consumer of `opacity.state-layer-hover` and the first component token to alias `spacing.56`.
